solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One taking steps spotted one pair outside

indicators.note: outside says the abbreviation for pair wraps round the other piece

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Someone out walking catches sight of a couple standing outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' is only a link here, meaning the pieces are found as described.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacer is a horse or runner that sets the stepping rhythm, so a stepper.

clue.text: Variety of herbal pies liable to go off

indicators.note: a variety is a mixed assortment, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A selection of herb-filled pies that may soon spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is likely to spoil or go bad is described as perishable.

clue.text: Tool was raised after series finished

indicators.note: after places the turned word behind the other piece

parts.note: a chain is a series of linked things

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: An implement was lifted once the run of episodes ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works because this is a down clue; 'finished' is just a link, the series being over before the tool follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chainsaw is a powered cutting implement, an example of a tool.

clue.text: He writes about beer

parts.note: RE is Latin for concerning, about
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A drinks columnist covers ales.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist is one whose job is writing up news stories.

clue.text: Spotty cloth Deb designed

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are freshly fashioned into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A debutante's dress fabric has a dotted pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotched skin or fabric is marked with spots or patches.

clue.text: Ice in November growing

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the following words, across the gap

explanation.surface: Frost builds up as winter approaches in the eleventh month.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg, shortened to berg, is a floating mass of ice.

clue.text: Chancy way of raising money

parts.note: reads like fundraising, but literally it is throwing a coin into the air to decide by chance

explanation.surface: A risky fundraising method for a charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Flipping a coin is a toss, and the outcome is a matter of even chance.

clue.text: Boastful words over the Atacama?

definitions.meaning: the air above a desert is literally hot

explanation.walkthrough: The Atacama is a desert in Chile, among the hottest and driest places on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is idiomatic for empty boasting; literally it hangs above a hot desert.

clue.text: Refuse to obey when fed up before end of day

indicators.note: before places this piece ahead of the next
in a down clue up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A diner who has had enough rebels as the day closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FED into DEF, and 'end of' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy authority is to refuse to obey it openly.

clue.text: Harvest fruit to be seen again

parts.note: to reap is to harvest
a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Gathering the orchard's crop so it shows up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappear is to come back into view, to be visible once more.

clue.text: A grossly distorted list of words

indicators.note: distorted says the letters are twisted out of their order

explanation.surface: A badly warped vocabulary list.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of terms with their meanings.

clue.text: Unlikely to appeal to pupils for a considerable time

definitions.meaning: a long school term is one that schoolchildren dislike
lasting or applying over a lengthy period

explanation.definitionFit: Long-term means extending over a lengthy period; read as two words it is a lengthy school term.

clue.text: A grain's polluting wine

indicators.note: polluting suggests the letters are corrupted and mixed up

parts.note: the letters of a grain plus the s of the possessive

explanation.surface: A cereal contaminates the vineyard's produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polluting' rearranges AGRAINS, the possessive s counting as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch made from red wine and fruit.

clue.text: Unqualified sailor thus has instrument

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
so means thus
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A seaman, it seems, owns a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means complete and without qualification or limit.

clue.text: Emperor heard to have broken rib

indicators.note: heard says the answer sounds like the phrase given

parts.note: a broken rib is a bone apart, split in two

explanation.surface: A ruler is said to have fractured a rib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard': a bone apart, said quickly, sounds like the French emperor's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was Emperor of the French.

clue.text: Sentiment about including lecturer during the enrolling

indicators.note: including says the abbreviation goes inside the rearranged letters
about suggests the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Feelings stir as a teacher joins in during sign-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges SENTIMENT, and 'including' puts L inside it; 'during' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlistment is the act of signing up, especially for military service.

clue.text: Trespassers will be charged?

parts.note: mimics a sign threatening prosecution, but the charging is done by an animal in the field

explanation.surface: A warning notice promising prosecution for intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: A field sign warning walkers that an aggressive animal may rush at them.

clue.text: The sot Erica in part difficult to understand

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of what the drunken Erica says is obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small specialist group, so obscure.

clue.text: Take covers off Sam unduly hot inside

indicators.note: inside says the rearranged letters go within the other piece

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies the USA

indicators.note: unduly suggests the letters are improperly ordered

explanation.surface: Strip the bedclothes off Sam, who is far too warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam is the personification of the United States, so 'Sam' alone stands for his title.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe is to remove someone's garments, their coverings.

clue.text: Earlier game piece found in treasury

parts.note: ex means former, earlier
a chequer is a piece in draughts

explanation.surface: An old game counter turns up in a museum's hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government department managing public funds, its treasury.

clue.text: Many order appropriate sweet

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
OM is the Order of Merit
fit means suitable, appropriate

explanation.surface: Plenty of people request a suitable dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A comfit is a sugar-coated sweet containing a nut or seed.

clue.text: Self-centredness, say, is in order

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: Putting oneself first is perfectly acceptable, they claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' is not an anagram signal here: it is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is a preoccupation with oneself, self-interest.

clue.text: Companion very much behind one who is at sea

indicators.note: behind puts this piece after the other

parts.note: a mate is a companion
a lot means very much

explanation.surface: A friend lags well behind a lost person.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang for a sailor, someone serving on ships.

clue.text: Extremely fast international winger

parts.note: reads like a speedy rugby wing, but the winger here is a large airliner

explanation.surface: A quick wing player who has been capped for his country.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-bodied airliner that flies international routes at high speed on its wings.

clue.text: Worthless craft

explanation.definitionFit: Junk is rubbish, and also a type of Chinese sailing vessel.

clue.text: Consider this container for body of experts

definitions.text: Consider this container for body of experts

parts.words: Consider this container for body of experts
parts.note: consider means think; putting it before this container makes the name of a policy research group

explanation.surface: An instruction to think about a vessel for a panel of specialists.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for liquid; with think in front it is a body of experts.

clue.text: Get irate damaging plume

indicators.note: damaging suggests the letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper wrecks a feathered hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is an ornamental feather tuft worn on a hat or headdress.

clue.text: Toy with distinguishing characteristic indicative of approval

definitions.note: the definition is descriptive; the answer is the symbol that shows approval

parts.note: a kite is a toy flown on a string
a mark is a distinguishing feature

explanation.surface: A plaything bearing a feature that signals it passed inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kitemark is the British Standards Institution's symbol certifying a product meets safety standards.

clue.text: Leading climber has breather on summit

indicators.note: leading picks out the first letter of the word climber

parts.note: a breather is a rest

explanation.surface: The mountaineer at the front pauses on reaching the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The crest of a hill or wave is its top, the summit.
